newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela labor reform to cost 1.8 pct GDP in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela labor reform to cost 1.8 pct GDP in 1997.

text.p: Implementing Venezuela's ground-breaking labor market and social security reforms will cost 1.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, government ministers said.
"That amount can be perfectly easily financed," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff told reporters after he presented a proposed reform of the Labor Law to Congress.

"We've studied the possible issue of internal debt to finance the additional cost." When quizzed by reporters, Petkoff did not disagree with estimates that put the total cost of the reform over five years at 12 percent of GDP.

The reforms would move Venezuela's crumbling social security system to a fully-funded system over five years and are expected to free-up rigid labor markets and lower company costs, so improving productivity throughout the economy.
But before the new system can be set up, the old system must be liquidated and workers paid accumulated severance pay.
Reform of the Labor Law is the first of a series of needed legislative changes. Debate is expected to be lengthy, although the government has said it hopes for passage by May 1.
